summary: troubleshooting@1.0.1 postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a 'Compatibility shim' and ships a trivial no-op Proxy as its main export, but also includes beacon.cjs which POSTs installer host identifiers (os.hostname(), __dirname install path, process.cwd(), process.version) to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon fires both from the postinstall lifecycle script (`node beacon.cjs`) and on require() via index.js, so simply installing or importing the package reports the host to the operator of that IP. The destination is a plaintext HTTP bare IP, not caller-configurable, and unrelated to any documented publisher infrastructure. The Proxy stub returning no-ops for all property accesses lets consuming builds continue to function so the install succeeds silently, which combined with the generic name and the beacon payload is the shape of a dependency-confusion / namespace-squat reconnaissance package harvesting internal build environments for follow-on targeting.
